articles.title: Patrick Mahomes Gets Win In Return: 3 Takeaways As Chiefs Beat Broncos
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs celebrated Patrick Mahomes' return with a win over the Denver Broncos on Monday night.
articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs closed Week 1 by turning back the clock. For at least one night, they looked like the AFC West's dominant force once again. After missing the playoffs, Kansas City came out of the gates in 2026 with a dominant win over the Denver Broncos, who won 14 games and were the AFC's No. 1 seed last season. The Chiefs defense caused fits, impressively containing a capable Broncos offense. Here are my takeaways: 1.Chiefs Look Like Contenders In Mahomes' Return Would the healthy return of Mahomes also mean the return of the Chiefs as the dangerous postseason threat you knew them to be? Mahomes made that clear from the first drive, taking off from the 15-yard line and diving into the end zone for a touchdown and an early lead on the Broncos. He got up in the end zone, brushed the proverbial dust off his chest and was back at home with the Arrowhead faithful. Overall, though, this was big-money acquisition Kenneth Walker’s night, with a 60-yard touchdown on the way to the best rushing game by a Chiefs running back in 14 years. In his Kansas City debut, Walker rushed for 173 yards and scored two total TDs. Was it vintage Mahomes? Of course not. He completed two of his first 12 passes for 14 yards but found a spark before halftime, and his defense really took care of the rest. Even a bad interception out of his own end zone that set Denver up at the 5-yard line only resulted in a field goal for the Broncos, with the Chiefs defense again stepping up to help the QB out. There was punctuation as well: On the first play of the fourth quarter, Mahomes found rookie running back Emmett Johnson for 25 yards on a third down, setting up a flip-toss touchdown to Walker for a 31-10 lead to put the game out of reach. Mahomes improved to 8-0 at home against Denver in his career, one of the longest home streaks for any quarterback against any opponent. After his shaky start, Mahomes went 11-for-13 for 145 yards and two touchdowns to pull away. Exactly one year earlier, the Chiefs had lost at home to the Eagles to fall to 0-2. They’d dig out of that to get to 5-3 before losing eight of their last nine in a wholly disappointing season. Are the Chiefs back as a pop-culture phenomenon? Taylor Swift was perched in a suite to cheer on her husband, Travis Kelce, on a 59-yard catch that was his longest in five years. Tom Cruise was sitting next to Swift, drawing cheers when he was shown on the stadium video boards. A surprisingly resounding Week 1 divisional win, combined with the Chargers’ wobbly start losing to Arizona, and just like that, the AFC West goes through Kansas City again. 2.Where Were Denver's Top Receivers? Denver gave up a first-round pick to land receiver Jaylen Waddle from Miami, and the hope was that Bo Nix would have more of a downfield passing game in 2026. That didn't take shape Monday night, as the Chiefs — despite losing rookie corner Mansoor Delane after one drive — effectively took Waddle and Courtland Sutton out of the game. Midway through the fourth quarter, the two receivers had combined for 13 yards on eight targets. Nix threw an interception on the opening drive, and there seemed to be a hesitation to gamble downfield, even with the Chiefs down a corner. A 19-yard touchdown to tight end Evan Engram was the only pass play longer than 13 yards entering the fourth quarter. Nix will get a better feel for Waddle, and they’ll connect as you’d expect. That didn’t happen when the Broncos needed it to on Monday night, though. 3.New Chiefs Secondary Doesn't Miss A Beat So much of Kansas City’s offseason was about departures in the secondary. Cornerback Trent McDuffie was traded to the Rams for a first-rounder, and fellow corner Jaylen Watson joined him in L.A. in free agency. Meanwhile, safety Bryan Cook signed with the Bengals. And yet the Chiefs' defense controlled the Broncos the entire game, even after losing Delane early. Kristian Fulton stepped up at corner, Nohl Williams had a sack, while L'Jarius Sneed had a great open-field tackle on Waddle on third-and-short. You go to seven Super Bowls, you’re going to get raided in free agency. For at least one game, though, the Chiefs don’t seem to be worse off at all. We’ll get to know these new players elevated into major roles, but they made a name for themselves keeping the Broncos in check Monday night. 3 ½. What's Next? Denver went 14-3 last year, and its upcoming schedule is daunting enough that it might have four losses by mid-October, without even really playing poorly. The Broncos’ next five games? Home vs. the Jaguars and Rams, at the 49ers and Chargers, then home against the Seahawks — all 2025 playoff teams expected to do the same this season. You could argue that the Chiefs, even at Arrowhead, were an easier opponent than any of those five. Denver could go from the top seed in the AFC and hosting a conference championship game to being under .500 at Halloween, unless they step up to a wildly difficult level of competition. Kansas City, meanwhile, will play next Sunday night at home against the Colts, who are 0-1 after a loss on Sunday to the Ravens. articles.title: Las gasolineras advierten: el litro de diésel podría superar los 2,20 euros el 1 de octubre
articles.standfirst: La patronal de las gasolineras prevé una subida de hasta 24 céntimos si el Gobierno deja caer las ayudas fiscales el 30 de septiembre.
articles.summary: La patronal de las gasolineras prevé una subida de hasta 24 céntimos si el Gobierno deja caer las ayudas fiscales el 30 de septiembre.
articles.body: El litro de gasóleo podría superar los 2,20 euros en algunas estaciones de servicio españolas. Hoy mismo el diésel se paga de media a 1,88 euros/litro y este escenario tan sangrante para muchas familias depende casi por completo de una fecha concreta, el 30 de septiembre. Esa fecha marca el final del actual paquete de ayudas fiscales a los carburantes, aprobado mediante el Real Decreto-ley 18/2026. El mecanismo incluye una rebaja sobre el Impuesto Especial sobre Hidrocarburos que ha ido reduciéndose mes a mes, desde los 20 céntimos de junio hasta los 5 previstos para septiembre. Y solo hay una posibilidad de que se mantenga algún tipo de descuento: si el IPC interanual de un carburante supera el 15%, la rebaja regresa por sí sola a los 20 céntimos. Eso fue justo lo que ocurrió con el gasóleo, cuya inflación llegó al 15,7% en julio y por eso nos libramos del subidón, mientras que la gasolina se quedó en un 7,3% y siguió el calendario ordinario hasta los 5 céntimos actuales. El peligro de que se puedan alcanzar o superar los 2,20 euros lo ha sacado a la luz la patronal del sector, la Confederación Española de Empresarios de Estaciones de Servicio (CEEES). Su director general, Nacho Rabadán, calcula que si el Gobierno deja caer la ayuda sin aprobar un nuevo decreto, el gasóleo subirá de golpe 24,4 céntimos el 1 de octubre. Y estos 24,4 céntimos salen de sumar los 20 céntimos de impuesto que desaparecen y el IVA correspondiente. Pero el tema fiscal sería solo una parte del problema, porque el gasóleo tiene también otros problemas. Las refinerías europeas trabajan cerca de su límite de capacidad, la oferta global de diésel escasea y el conflicto en Oriente Medio ha dañado varias infraestructuras clave, lo que ha disparado las cotizaciones del gasóleo hasta niveles nunca vistos. De todas formas, el Gobierno aún puede aprobar un nuevo Real Decreto antes de que acabe septiembre o ampliar el actual. Hay que tener en cuenta que, pese a la rebaja de 20 céntimos que entró en vigor el 1 de septiembre, el gasóleo ha subido unos 5 céntimos en apenas diez días, señal de que la presión al alza del mercado internacional ya se está comiendo buena parte del descuento. Si ese ritmo se mantiene, el litro rondará los 2 euros de media justo el día 30 de septiembre, el último con la ayuda todavía en vigor, y a partir de ahí entraría de golpe la subida de más de 20 céntimos. Pese a todo, todavía estamos lejos de los precios que se pagan en algunos países europeos, como Finlandia, Países Bajos o Dinamarca, donde el litro de diésel ya se paga por encima de los 2,40 euros/litro. Pero una subida como la que tenemos nos iría acercando poco a poco a los precios de estos países.

articles.title: What does Toto Wolff see in George Russell that keeps him believing in the Mercedes star despite his difficult 2026 F1 season?
articles.summary: International Sports News: George Russell’s 2026 Formula 1 campaign has taken a sharp turn, but Toto Wolff is looking beyond the points table. The Mercedes driver has fallen 81 .
articles.body: George Russell’s 2026 Formula 1 campaign has taken a sharp turn, but Toto Wolff is looking beyond the points table. The Mercedes driver has fallen 81 points behind teammate Kimi Antonelli after a difficult run that has weakened his championship challenge. Russell has already admitted that winning the title is now extremely unlikely. Wolff, however, continues to describe him as a top driver with the ability to fight for championships. His support comes at a difficult moment, but it also reveals something important about how Mercedes views Russell. For Wolff, the current results are a setback, not a final judgment on the driver’s ability.From karting championships to Mercedes success, Toto Wolff sees the proven winner still hidden behind George Russell’s difficult 2026 seasonRussell’s recent form has made his championship situation difficult to ignore. His fifth-place finish at the Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid came as Antonelli secured another victory and stretched his advantage over his Mercedes teammate.The gap has grown dramatically. Antonelli has added 56 points to his advantage over Russell across the last five races, turning a 25-point deficit into an 81-point one.Russell understands the situation better than anyone. After the Spanish Grand Prix, he admitted that his title hopes had suffered a major blow.“I won’t say it’s over, but it's extremely unlikely I’ll be in that fight,” the 28-year-old admitted.Wolff, however, does not believe Russell should be judged only by what has happened during this difficult stretch.“When it comes to George, you can have good races, bad races, good years, and bad years, but we're talking about the driver that has won everything that you could have potentially won before.“Every single karting championship, Formula 3 in his rookie year, Formula 2 in his rookie year, went into the Williams. I mean, we're talking about a top driver.Those achievements help explain Wolff’s confidence. Russell did not arrive in Formula 1 without a proven record. He had already established himself as a winner through the junior categories before joining Williams and eventually earning his Mercedes seat.For Wolff, that history is evidence that Russell has the ability to perform at the highest level even if his current season is not showing it.Why Toto Wolff believes George Russell can recover mentally and return to the F1 championship fightWolff’s support goes beyond Russell’s racing record. The Mercedes boss also believes the psychological pressure of a difficult season has played a role in the driver’s struggles.“We need to find out what it is for him to be able to unleash that potential, and of course there's the psychological side. If you have a run like him this year, you're taking a beating, but the great ones, they recover, and I think that George has all he needs to fight for championships," Wolff explained.The comment is significant because Wolff is acknowledging the pressure Russell has faced instead of pretending that everything is normal. A driver repeatedly losing ground to his teammate can quickly lose confidence, especially when championship expectations were much higher earlier in the season.Yet Wolff believes the response to that pressure could ultimately define Russell’s season.The Mercedes team principal also refuses to completely dismiss Russell’s title chances while a mathematical route remains.“It’s a mechanical sport. You can DNF, you can crash out, and it happens two times in a row, and then suddenly what looked like a nice buffer is not anymore because you have six races to go.“So in my opinion, we just need to ignore the points until it is mathematically not realistic anymore, or not real anymore for them to win, and until then just concentrate on each and every weekend, try to bring your best game.That approach gives Russell a simpler target. Instead of allowing the 81-point gap to dominate the remainder of his season, he can focus on producing stronger performances and helping Mercedes in the Constructors’ Championship.Antonelli currently has the momentum, but Wolff’s belief in Russell has not disappeared. Mercedes is already working toward 2027, giving Russell another chance to reset and show that his difficult 2026 season does not define his championship potential.For Wolff, the question is not whether Russell has the talent to fight for titles. articles.title: Fantasy Football Waiver Wire Pickups, Week 2: Kaelon Black, Denzel Boston among top targets to add
articles.summary: Justin Boone takes you through his top players to add off the waiver wire for fantasy football in Week 2.
articles.body:
Every Monday during the season, Justin Boone breaks down the recommended waiver-wire pickups.

Roster percentages are generated from Yahoo leagues. Free-Agent Budget (FAB) amounts are based on a $100 salary cap. Only players rostered in less than 50% of leagues are considered.

Young is coming off an outstanding fantasy performance in the opener, when he threw for 361 yards, three touchdowns and one pick, while adding 10 yards and a score on the ground.

The emergence of Jalen Coker gives Young another dangerous weapon to pair with Tetairoa McMillan in the passing game. Even veteran tight end Darren Waller should see his role grow as he gets more comfortable in Carolina's offense. Waller had a touchdown called back in his Panthers' debut on Sunday due to a penalty.

Next up for Young is a Falcons defense that he's had plenty of success against in recent years — especially in Atlanta, where this game will be played. Young has thrown three touchdown passes in each of his past two trips to Mercedes-Benz Stadium, including a 448-yard, three-TD effort in November. After this game, he gets the always struggling Browns and a banged up Lions' secondary.

Risky streaming options (if starter is out)

Desperation streaming options (if healthy)

With Christian McCaffrey racking up 450 touches last year (including playoffs) and entering his age-30 season, rostering his backup is an important move in fantasy. That's why I spent most of the summer recommending Black as a late-round target.

It seems like Kyle Shanahan also recognized the risk involved with giving McCaffrey another massive workload, because the 49ers split their backfield snaps 36-28 in the opener. While CMC poured in 88 scrimmage yards on 15 touches, Black wasn't far behind with 70 yards on 16 chances.

It's possible the split was the result of McCaffrey missing time in August due to injury or the fact the game was played in Australia. Regardless, it's clear that Black is the one-injury-away option in San Francisco and he could offer weekly flex value if the team continues to get him involved. Most importantly, Black looked good on his carries.

The rookie will be an RB3/flex option in a Week 2 matchup where the 49ers are 13-point favorites over the Dolphins.

The Broncos play on Monday Night Football, so we've to see how they plan to deploy their backfield. There's a wide range of outcomes for Coleman, who could have a role right away or be brought along slowly as the J.K. Dobbins insurance plan.

Regardless, he needs to be rostered everywhere. Dobbins is healthy entering the season and we all hope this is the year he finally plays all 17 games. However, history has taught us otherwise as the veteran missed time due to injuries in all six of his NFL campaigns. Though RJ Harvey is the No. 2 back on Denver's depth chart, it's Coleman who projects to benefit the most if Dobbins goes to the blue medical tent again.

Sean Payton has raved about the rookie, even comparing his skillset to Dobbins. In the event of another injury, Coleman is the most likely to step into the lead-back role, while Harvey maintains his change-of-pace, pass-catching back usage. Don't wait until Dobbins gets hurt, scoop Coleman up now.

Tyler Allegeier is 51% rostered but would be the No. 3 RB add behind Black and Coleman, if available.

Zach Charbonnet is 50% rostered but can be added as an IR stash, if available.

Best one-injury away backup RBs to stash

The Browns' passing attack is definitely a work in progress with a potentially volatile depth chart at quarterback. Even in a Week 1 matchup with the Jaguars where the offense floundered for most of the game, their two rookie receivers managed to flash.

First-rounder KC Concepcion caught four of his five targets for 43 yards, while earning three carries for 15 yards. Unfortunately, he had his debut marred by a fumble. It was actually Cleveland's second-round selection Boston who came away with the better fantasy afternoon, turning his four targets into 59 yards and a touchdown, which accounted for 46 of those yards. Boston also led the Browns wideouts in snaps by a wide margin, taking the field for 92% of their offensive plays.

We have a long way to go before having faith in a Deshaun Watson-led passing game, but fantasy managers would be wise to hold the Browns rookie wideouts to see how much Todd Monken can get out of this group as the season moves along.

Even amid the struggles of the Dolphins offense in Week 1, Douglas had an impressive debut. The third-round rookie played 91% of the snaps, catching five of his seven targets for 94 yards.

We knew the opportunity was there for someone to emerge in Miami's no-name receiver room and Douglas made a strong case to be that guy in the opener. His teammate, Malik Washington, is also a potential flex option and I'm still stashing fellow third rounder Chris Bell, whom I believe is the better talent. However, it's impossible to ignore this effort from Douglas.

Rookies who look like they belong right away are the exact kind of early-season waiver wire pickups you want to be aggressively adding.

With Chris Olave in and out of their Week 1 contest due to cramps and falling hard on his back, Vele led the Saints receivers with a 91% snap share.

In the extremely high-volume matchup with the Lions, the 28-year-old drew nine targets, which he turned into a 7-69-1 stat line. Though it's hard to project that kind of volume on a weekly basis, the Saints were No. 1 in neutral offensive pace last season and will likely be among the league leaders in that category again.

First-rounder Jordyn Tyson remains on injured reserve for at least another three weeks and it's possible his hamstring injury could sidelined him until midseason. In the meantime, Vele is a sneaky flex option in Kellen Moore's offense.

Deebo Samuel Sr. is 50% rostered but would be the No. 1 WR add, if available.

Jakobi Meyers is 51% rostered but would be the No. 4 WR add behind Samuel, Boston and Douglas, if available.

Romeo Doubs is 54% rostered but would be the No. 6 WR add behind Samuel, Boston, Douglas, Meyers and Vele, if available.

Jordyn Tyson is 55% rostered but can be added as an IR stash, if available.

If you're looking for a streamer, you might want to consider Dalton Schultz or Brenton Strange this week. However, if your goal is to a potential season-long breakout at the position — you should target Sadiq.

Despite missing time this summer while recovering from offseason sports hernia surgery, the first-round tight end was active in Week 1 and made an impact. The coaching staff stayed true to their plan of working him back into the lineup slowly, but Sadiq earned just as many targets as teammate Mason Taylor (three) and caught all of them 21 yards. Even more intriguing was his three-yard, goal-line carry, which resulted in his first career touchdown.

According to beat writers, Sadiq was getting a lot of volume in practice before his injury and this was a great sign the team will find ways to get the ball in his hands moving forward. With fellow first-rounder Omar Cooper Jr. dealing with a high-ankle sprain that may cost him a few weeks, Sadiq could see his target share rise quickly.

Hunter Henry is 54% rostered but would be the No. 1 TE add if available.

Terrance Ferguson vs. NYG (23% rostered)

Favorable upcoming schedules: Chiefs Defense (12% rostered), Packers defense (15% rostered), Panthers defense (1% rostered)

Here are some players you can consider cutting from your roster to free up room on your bench for this week's top waiver-wire adds.

Quarterbacks: Baker Mayfield, Sam Darnold

Running Backs: Kenny Gainwell, Rachaad White

Wide Receivers: Rashid Shaheed, Ja'Kobi Lane

It's difficult to drop any running back, since their value could increase with an injury or two. However, based on what we saw in Week 1, I'm worried about the role for Gainwell and White in their respective offenses. The hope that they could be weekly flex plays is dwindling. Even if their starters get hurt, we would likely see another back form a committee with them.

Meanwhile, with the injury to Sam Darnold, Shaheed is no longer as enticing and can be sent to the waiver wire. He may still have some boom weeks, but he can't be trusted in your lineup. And if you don't have room to stash Lane on IR when he's ruled out due to the wrist injury, you can let him go as well.

articles.title: 49ers are favorites to win the NFC West, but Rams remain favorites to win the Super Bowl
articles.summary: The 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams resulted in a shift in betting odds, but perhaps not as big a shift as some would think.
articles.body:
The 49ers ' Week 1 win over the Rams resulted in a shift in betting odds, but perhaps not as big a shift as some would think.

The Rams remain the favorites to win the Super Bowl, as they were before the season. The Rams' Super Bowl odds dropped to +650 from their preseason odds of +500 , but they're still the favorites to win it all.

The 49ers, however, are now the favorites to win the NFC West. The 49ers' odds are +160 to win the division, followed by the Seahawks at +175 and Rams at +205. The Cardinals are extreme long shots at +4500.

The 49ers' odds to win the Super Bowl are +1400, tied with the Chiefs for the fifth-best chance of winning the title.

Why would the Rams be first in Super Bowl odds but third in division odds? It's ultimately about how good the oddsmakers think the Rams will be by the time the postseason rolls around. Right now, with Myles Garrett on injured reserve and Aaron Donald yet to play, it's easy to see the Rams starting slow and falling behind in the division. But if they make the playoffs at all, the Rams should be a tough team to beat.

The Rams may have to go on the road in the playoffs, but no one should dismiss their chances of winning it all.

articles.title: Jerrod Johnson Reveals the One Thing Eagles’ Offense Must Do To Keep QB Playing Fast
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles opened the season with a win; however, the offense didn’t exactly cruise through it. The Eagles beat the Washington Commanders 24-22,...
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles opened the season with a win; however, the offense didn't exactly cruise through it. The Eagles beat the Washington Commanders 24-22, but there were enough protection and execution issues to leave questions heading into Week 2.

Jalen Hurts was able to make plays when things broke down; however, the offense also had stretches where the Commanders created pressure and disrupted the timing of the attack, and with a new offensive staff in place, finding a way to keep Hurts comfortable and decisive will be a big part of the early-season adjustment.

Jerrod Johnson Explains What Philadelphia Eagles Need From Their Offense

On September 15, the current Eagles senior offensive analyst, Jerrod Johnson, explained what he believes is the key to helping a quarterback play fast. Speaking to Steelers Takeaways, Johnson focused on what happens before the ball even gets to the QB.

"I think everything goes through the eyes of the quarterback. If you can make defenses have to cover every inch of grass that's important – while allowing the quarterback to still play fast. If you can manipulate the defense and allow the quarterback to play free – that's the key. "

For the Eagles, that approach matters even more with the offensive line still finding its footing. They allowed three sacks against the Commanders, while the run game produced 136 yards but relied heavily on Saquon Barkley 's 42-yard burst.

Landon Dickerson is also now headed to injured reserve, meaning the Eagles will have to make another adjustment up front. The head coach, Nick Sirianni, confirmed Tuesday that the team already has a direction in mind for replacing him, but did not reveal who will get the job.

Johnson's point goes beyond one positio n group, though. He believes the offense has to give its QB answers without slowing him down. The defense should be forced to defend the full field, while Hurts needs to recognize what is happening and get the ball out quickly.

That fits with Johnson's broader philosophy as a quarterback coach. He listed accuracy and processing speed among the most important traits at the position, with mobility also becoming increasingly valuable as defenses get better.

It's safe to say that the Eagles have many things to clean up after Week 1, but one thing is sure: they won the game. Seven punts and three sacks were enough to show how fast the offense could get out of rhythm.

Now, the most important thing is to make sure that the issues will not make Hurts play at a speed he shouldn't be playing. If the Eagles are going to put more pressure on the defense of their opponents without putting Hurts under pressure, everything will be fine.

articles.title: Celtics predicted to trade Paul George for $240M high-scoring duo to pair with Jayson Tatum
articles.summary: The Boston Celtics are still looking for ways to bolster the roster. In this trade idea, they get two young players to help compete in the Eastern Conference...
articles.body:
The Boston Celtics have had quite the offseason in terms of moves made, which is weird considering it involved getting rid of their Finals MVP. It was an interesting move, but one that was somewhat warranted, as Jaylen Brown has been involved in trade talks for years.

There was plenty of reasoning for why things went down the way they did. However, Jayson Tatum's camp was not real happy with Brown.

"Members of Tatum's camp had expressed externally to others in league circles that they were not happy with Brown's demeanor and his angle of claiming that this was the season he enjoyed the most with the Celtics," NBA insider Brett Siegel said.

For this reason, Boston decided to find a trade suitor for Brown. The Celtics sent their Finals MVP to the Philadelphia 76ers for Paul George .

"Jaylen Brown has a new home, as the Boston Celtics agreed to send the former NBA Finals MVP to the Philadelphia 76ers in a blockbuster trade Wednesday, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. The 76ers are sending Paul George, two first-round picks (2028, 2031) and two second-round selections (2028, 2030) to Boston to complete the deal, sources said," ESPN wrote.

It was kind of a strange deal. Heavy.com's Adam Taylor has created a trade package that sends George to the New Orleans Pelicans for Trey Murphy III and Jordan Poole .

"Celtics Get: Jordan Poole, Trey Murphy. Pelicans Get: Paul George, a 2032 first-round draft pick, a 2030 first-round pick swap, a 2031 first-round pick swap, a 2030 second-round pick and a 2032 second-round pick," Taylor wrote.

Boston would be getting significantly better, and their bench would be great. Derrick White and Payton Pritchard would start, then be followed by Murphy and Poole.

Poole and Murphy's contracts combine for $240 million. Both players can score at any time, and Murphy is great on the defensive end. If this trade went down, the Celtics will have turned Brown into Poole and Murphy.

articles.title: Rashee Rice emphasizes Chiefs’ physicality on display against Broncos
articles.summary: Kansas City’s wideout can feel the change the team made on offense this offseason.
articles.body:
On the surface, the wide receivers on either side of the field in the Kansas City Chiefs ' 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos were not impactful. The Chiefs' offense ran through tailback Kenneth Walker , who filled up the box score; Walker accounted for 49% of Kansas City's total yards on "Monday Night Football."

However, the Chiefs' No. 1 receiver was all smiles when speaking to Voice of the Chiefs Mitch Holthus on the team's official postgame show , "Chiefs Rewind," on YouTube . Rashee Rice scored a touchdown after breaking tackles near the goal line, but he finished with just two catches and 19 yards.

He made a point to affect the game without the ball in his hands.

On the 59-yard gain by tight end Travis Kelce in the third quarter, moving the chains on a crucial third down, Rice can be seen blocking downfield with great effort, preventing the Broncos' cornerback from getting in on the tackle that brought Kelce down inside the five-yard line.

"We ran that ball, and we blocked downfield for everybody to have the ball in their hands," Rice told Holthus. "We definitely blocked for our brothers today."

Rice, who led all Chiefs receivers in offensive snaps, usually blocked for a handoff to Kenneth Walker on his way to a league-leading 173 rushing yards. With the team's new talent in the backfield, Rice is learning that, similar to quarterback Patrick Mahomes' relentlessness on a dropback, Walker has a chance to break into the third level of a defense on every touch.

"It's hard to not watch those guys while the ball is in their hands," Rice acknowledged. "It's hard to go get your assignment because those guys are so fun to watch. Sometimes, you get caught up being on the backside of a play, just watching them run the ball — then out of nowhere, [Walker] comes to the backside with the ball in his hands and you have to find a second effort to block the guy in front of you."

Despite the Chiefs' abysmal downfield passing attack in Week 1, Rice understands what Walker's big game can do for the unit moving forward.

"We have somebody there that's going to affect the defense," Rice said of Walker. "It's going to leave us one-on-one with certain defenders and cornerbacks, so having a running back like that is huge for the offense."

It all comes back to the team's identity shift this offseason, which was headlined by the re-hire of offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy. The team is clearly more physical, and Rice — in his first season under Bieniemy's coaching — can see the difference.

"I think we're a much more physical team than I've been on throughout these past three years," Rice told Matt Derrick of Chiefs Digest in the locker room after the game . "I think that comes with the coaching."

"I love it," Rice emphasized. "[It's a] mentality."

articles.title: Iowa football rises in latest USA TODAY Sports 1-138 Re-Rank
articles.summary: After a Cy-Hawk victory, the Hawkeyes rose in the latest 1-138 re-rank from USA Today.
articles.body:
After starting the 2026 season outside the top 25 of the initial USA TODAY Sports NCAA 1-138 Re-Rank, Iowa made its way up to 24th after a Week 1 victory.

Following a hard-fought win in the Cy-Hawk game on Saturday, the Hawkeyes saw their stock rise even higher this week.

A new edition of the USA TODAY Sports NCAA 1-138 Re-Rank dropped on Monday following a wild Week 2. Iowa rose one spot from last week, ending up at 23rd on this week's ranking. They're just ahead of Oklahoma , which dropped 15 spots after losing in Ann Arbor over the weekend.

It wasn't a pretty performance for Iowa on Saturday. They didn't play their best game and received quite the challenge from a hungry Iowa State team. articles.title: Referees chief Webb 'really disappointed' over VAR error in Manchester derby
articles.summary: Referees' chief Howard Webb said he was "really disappointed" with the VAR mistake that allowed Erling Haaland's winner in the Manchester derby last weekend....
articles.body:
Referees' chief Howard Webb said he was "really disappointed" with the VAR mistake that allowed Erling Haaland 's winner in the Manchester derby last weekend.

Haaland scored in the second half of City's victory against arch rivals United at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Haaland's close-range finish from Josko Gvardiol 's cross was initially disallowed for offside, but VAR official Matt Donohue and his assistant Blake Antrobus overturned the decision.

Donohue ruled City midfielder Enzo Fernandez was not interfering with play when he tried to reach the ball before it was finished off by Haaland.

City went on to win 1-0, but the result was overshadowed by the controversy involving the decisive goal.

United manager Michael Carrick said he was "staggered" by the decision because Fernandez blocked Lisandro Martinez 's attempt to clear and potentially distracted goalkeeper Senne Lammens .

Donohue and Antrobus have been stood down by the Pro Ref organisation for this weekend's Premier League matches.

Webb, the chief refereeing officer at Pro Ref, said on the 'Match Officials: Mic'd Up' programme on Tuesday: "I was really disappointed with this outcome. We all are. None more so than the officials themselves.

"They take a lot of personal pride in what they do and they're obviously hurting now, having fallen short in this situation.

"They'll not be officiating again until after the international break. We've reached out to Manchester United and acknowledged the error, as we do when these things happen."

Asked how the VAR officials had come to the conclusion that Fernandez was not interfering with play, Webb said: "In that moment, he (Donohue) gets tunnel vision.

"He gets focused on Haaland, and it's down to the rest of his team to pull him out of that tunnel, and unfortunately, that didn't happen on this occasion.

"This goal should have been disallowed. We'll review it, reflect upon it, and try to take the learning forward to prevent this unusual type of error from happening again."

articles.title: VAR did not even consider if Fernandez was offside - Webb
articles.summary: Referees' chief Howard Webb has admitted that the video assistant referee (VAR) did not even consider whether Enzo Fernandez was offside for Erling Haaland's...
articles.body:
Referees' chief Howard Webb has admitted that the video assistant referee (VAR) did not even consider whether Enzo Fernandez was offside for Erling Haaland 's controversial winner in Sunday's Manchester derby.

Speaking on the first edition of 'Match Officials Mic'd Up' of the season, Webb said he was "really disappointed" with the error made by the VAR Matt Donohue and his assistant Blake Antrobus.

Manchester City striker Haaland thought he had scored the only goal of the game at Old Trafford in the 60th minute, but it was disallowed on the field for offside.

A VAR review found Haaland was just onside, and the goal was awarded.

But it immediately became apparent that the video officials had made an error in failing to identify an offside offence by Fernandez, diving at the ball in a central position and interfering with opponents.

"I was really disappointed with this outcome. We all are," said Webb, Premier League refereeing body Pro Ref's chief refereeing officer.

"None more so than the officials themselves. They take a lot of personal pride in what they do and they're obviously hurting now, having fallen short in this situation.

"They'll not be officiating again until after the international break."

One of the questions which many supporters have asked is how the VAR team could possibly reach the conclusion that Fernandez did not commit an offside offence.

Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez initially appeared to be marking Haaland, but then moved over to try and intercept the ball from Fernandez. This left Haaland free at the back post to finish.

Former England striker and BBC Sport pundit Wayne Rooney said on Match of the Day that "to not see that and recognise that Enzo Fernandez was in an offside position...anyone who has played the game at any level understands that and to get it so wrong is baffling."

The Mic'd Up audio revealed that at no stage did Donohue or Antrobus consider whether Fernandez was offside because, as Webb describes, they got "tunnel vision" over Haaland.

The semi-automated offside technology told the VAR that Haaland was three centimetres onside from Josko Gvardiol's cross.

But the video officials then only checked for a touch by Fernandez which would have created a new offside phase against the Norway international .

"The VAR gets super-focused on Haaland," said Webb, who had already been in contact with Manchester United to share the VAR audio and video.

"He establishes he's onside, he thinks that's a good goal.

"He doesn't truly evaluate the full impact of Fernandez's position. He has a look to see if he touches the ball, because then that relates to potentially knocking it to Haaland, who goes on to score.

"In that moment, he gets tunnel vision. It's down to the rest of his team to pull him out of that tunnel, and unfortunately, that didn't happen on this occasion.

"What looks like a really clear subjective offside, because Fernandez doesn't touch the ball but still clearly impacts [the play but] doesn't get identified, and it's really disappointing.

"This goal should've been disallowed. And highly unfortunately, it wasn't, and we'll review it, reflect upon it, and try to take the learning forward to prevent this unusual type of error from happening again."

Fernandes is 'more petulant than violent'

There was also much debate over the red card shown to Phil Foden in the 23th minute for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes, largely because there was no sanction against the Portuguese midfielder for a similar act.

Webb backed the decision to dismiss Foden, but said the action by Fernandes did not meet the threshold for violent conduct.

"I agree with the red card for Phil Foden," said Webb. "He kicks out with force into the upper body of Bruno Fernandes.

"Now, when you look at the footage, there is that petulant kick by Bruno Fernandes into the backside of Foden. It is more petulant than violent.

"To be violent conduct, it has to have excessive force or brutality. When you look at that, particularly in full speed, it doesn't have those elements. So therefore, this would be a yellow card offence."

Webb added that if Foden had not been sent off on the field, but he had been via a VAR review - as Aston Villa 's Joao Gomes was at Brighton for a similar offence last month - Fernandes' yellow-card offence would also have been identified at the pitchside monitor.

articles.title: 📈 From 3. Liga to Germany? He could solve Klopp's biggest problem
articles.summary: Hardly any German professional footballer has enjoyed such a rapid rise in recent years as Philipp Treu. Just three years ago, the right-back was still playi...
articles.body:
Hardly any German professional footballer has enjoyed such a rapid rise in recent years as Philipp Treu . Just three years ago, the right-back was still playing in the 3. Liga. Back then, nothing — truly nothing — suggested that he would one day feature for the German national team . But things have changed.

Treu never took the quick route, always the logical next step instead. From captain of SC Freiburg 's second team, he became a Bundesliga player at FC St. Pauli , before returning to Breisgau in the summer of 2025 after two years at the Millerntor — this time, however, as part of the senior squad.

The 25-year-old quickly developed into a key player at the second attempt and was one of the faces of last season's hugely successful campaign. Sport-Club reached the Europa League final and once again qualified for Europe through the league. Treu was always a reliable presence throughout. Across all competitions, he made 46 appearances.

Quietly and without much fuss, the calls for a DFB call-up therefore grew louder. It was not enough for a place in the World Cup squad, however, as Julian Nagelsmann opted against taking the dynamic full-back to the USA, Canada and Mexico .

Will DFB captain Kimmich benefit from Treu?

A few months later — after another botched DFB tournament and a strong start to the season for Freiburg — the tide now seems to have turned. Treu has every chance of being among the chosen few of new Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp. And this is where the whole story gets really exciting: the Freiburg man might not just be a bit-part player for the four-time world champions, but rather an immediate solution to a problem. His biggest asset is that he is a classic right-back.

Because Germany's perhaps biggest squad issue goes by the name of Joshua Kimmich — ironically, perhaps their most reliable player. Not because the Bayern star is too poor despite some disappointing tournaments. Quite the opposite. Rather, it is because he is at his most valuable in central midfield.

That is where Kimmich has played for Bayern for years, where he organizes the game, dictates the tempo and takes responsibility. In the DFB team, by contrast, he has almost always had to fill in in the back four because of a lack of viable alternatives. In that role, however, Kimmich's athletic shortcomings have repeatedly been exposed. At the same time, Germany's midfield lacked its most dominant tempo-setter.

Under Klopp, the 31-year-old is now likely to return to the engine room. Treu, in turn, is among the most promising candidates to take over the then-vacant spot on the right side of defence. The Heidelberg native can play at high intensity and puts in a sharp shift both going forward and at the back.

Treu himself, by the way, has made no secret of his ambitions. In recent months, he has spoken several times about his dream of one day wearing the eagle on his chest. "In any case, we don't have all that many options at full-back in Germany," he said in a March interview with kicker.

Speaking to Sky ahead of Thursday's squad announcement, the Freiburg player also revealed a phone call with Jürgen Klopp. "I had a FaceTime call with the national coach. It was a cool conversation to get an idea of what his plan is. I can only say positive things. Whether it'll be enough on Thursday, we'll see."

The dream of a first DFB call-up therefore seems more within reach than ever.

articles.title: NHL Teams Scramble to Lock In 8-Year Deals Before New CBA Kicks In
articles.summary: Teams are pushing to sign players to max-length contracts before terms drop.
articles.body:
NHL teams are in the final hours to re-sign players to eight-year deals before the max contract extension drops by a year. The league's new CBA, negotiated between the NHL and NHLPA last summer, kicks in at midnight on Sept. 16. It stipulates that players can only sign seven-year deals with their existing teams (and six with new teams, also down a year from prior rules).

Teams have been busy in the final hours before the deadline.

Tuesday morning, eight-year contracts were announced for Capitals winger Ryan Leonard , 21; Senators winger Drake Batherson , 28; and Sabres center Noah Östlund, 22. All begin for the 2027–28 season.

A flurry of other deals landed in August and early September, most notably for Cale Makar and the Avalanche. Colorado locked up the 27-year-old defenseman for eight years in an agreement worth $163.2 million at a $20.4 million AAV—the richest in NHL history .

The new CBA's surging salary cap has particularly been a windfall for emerging stars who want a guaranteed payday through a long-term deal, even in an era where franchises will have more and more cash to play with.

As the clock ticks down to the midnight changeover, and more deals may land, eyes are particularly on a few players who have yet to sign extensions: among them, Minnesota 's Quinn Hughes , Anaheim 's Cutter Gauthier , Columbus's Adam Fantilli , and San Jose's Will Smith . (Younger players, including Sharks superstar Macklin Celebrini , have recently re-upped with their teams on shorter agreements.)

The new NHL CBA, which begins as training camps open tomorrow, will bring more changes. Among them are an extended season with 84 games instead of 82 and a shorter preseason; the creation of a playoff salary cap; the elimination of deferred compensation; and a formal nixing of the league's dress code .

articles.title: ‘I Don’t Understand’ — Browns Hosts Blast Fans Blaming Media for Deshaun Watson-Shedeur Sanders Decision
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns’ quarterback situation has somehow become even louder after one game. Deshaun Watson definitely had an off day for the Browns against th...
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns' quarterback situation has somehow become even louder after one game. Deshaun Watson definitely had an off day for the Browns against the Jacksonville Jaguars when opening the new NFL season, but Shedeur Sanders is still the man that the fans keep mentioning whenever the Browns' offense sputters. But now, the discussion has shifted from Watson's play to whether anyone ever wanted Watson to be quarterback in the first place.

This discussion did not go over well with radio hosts Ken Carman and Anthony Lima on the Cleveland station 92.3 The Fan. The discussion on the radio program on September 15 was regarding fans blaming the media for wanting Watson to play over Sanders in light of Sunday's events.

Ken Carman And Anthony Lima Push Back On Watson-Sanders Narrative

The Browns made their choice before Week 1. Head coach Todd Monken handed Watson the starting job over Sanders, giving him another opportunity after his long injury absence; however, Watson's first regular-season outing did little to calm the noise.

"I don't understand where the hell that Sunday performance had anything to do with, 'oh, you're wearing this now'…"

The Browns lost 34-10 to the Jaguars, with Watson completing 11 of 17 passes for 100 yards and an interception through the first three quarters. He did throw a 46-yard touchdown pass late; however, much of his production came after the Jaguars had already built a huge lead.

That brought the criticism back quickly. Some fans blamed the Browns for choosing Watson, while others pushed the idea that media members had wanted him to win the QB battle; however, the Cleveland radio host was not buying that explanation

C arman and Lima were specifically responding to fans claiming the media wanted Watson to start instead of Sanders. The point was pretty simple: Watson's Week 1 performance created its own discussion, and there was already plenty of history behind the reaction. Watson entered the season having played only 19 games for the Browns since joining the team in 2022. His stint has been interrupted by injuries, while his production has fallen well short of what the Browns expected when they gave him a fully guaranteed $230 million contract.

The preseason had already shown how tense the relationship with fans had become. Watson was booed at the Browns home stadium, and he later said the reaction felt personal.

Monken, meanwhile, has repeatedly f ramed the QB decision around football. He said the staff's job is to put the player on the field who gives Cleveland the best chance to win. That puts Watson in a tough spot heading into Week 2. The Browns are still sticking with him against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , while Sanders remains the obvious name waiting behind him.

However, after the Jacksonville loss, the conversation is no longer just about who should start but also about how long Cleveland can keep Watson there if the results do not change.

Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr acknowledged that the possibility of LeBron James joining the organization never appeared particularly realistic before the superstar ultimately signed with the Philadelphia 76ers this offseason.

With the 2026-27 NBA season approaching, Kerr discussed Golden State's connection to James during the latest episode of the "Tom Tolbert Show." The Warriors coach joked that he "doesn't think he'll get fined" for admitting that James' potential move to the Bay Area felt more like outside speculation than an impending transaction.

"I don't think it's exactly earthshattering news or I don't think I'll get fined for saying like it never really felt like he was, you know, coming here," Kerr said. "It was more speculation than anything. I think we would have had a much better sense that, you know, something was going to happen."

Kerr also revealed that Warriors fans have approached him since James' decision and expressed relief that the longtime Golden State rival did not join the franchise.

"It's been really interesting though hearing fans around the Bay," Kerr said. "Like, you know, people will randomly come up to me and say, 'I'm glad we didn't get Bron' and I'm like, really? And they're like, 'Yeah, it's like he's not supposed to be on our team. He's a rival.'"

Steve Kerr was open to coaching LeBron James with Warriors

James developed a lengthy rivalry with the Warriors during his second stint with the Cleveland Cavaliers, facing Golden State in four consecutive NBA Finals from 2015 through 2018 .

Kerr compared the idea of James joining Golden State to other legendary rivals eventually becoming teammates.

"And I get that as a sports fan," Kerr said. "It'd be like, should Magic and Bird have played on the same team? So, I mean, just as a coach and having coached him in the Olympics, sign me up!"

The possibility of James joining the Warriors generated attention earlier in the offseason. A fan posted a video of his family's encounter with Kerr and told the coach that Golden State needed to acquire James.

Kerr responded with a tongue-in-cheek message.

"Oh, we got him. Put that on Twitter," Kerr said.

That prediction did not become reality. James instead signed with the Philadelphia 76ers , leaving Golden State without the blockbuster addition.

articles.body:
Anfield Fear Factor Fading as Liverpool Home Form Raises Serious Questions

Anfield used to do half the job before kick-off. Opponents arrived knowing the noise would be relentless, the pressure immediate and the margin for error tiny. That edge has dulled. The numbers say so, the eye test says so, and now former elite players are saying it out loud.

Liverpool have drawn at home with Nottingham Forest and Fulham in the opening month of the season. Across the 2026 calendar year, they have won only four of 12 Premier League matches at Anfield. That is not a blip, it is a pattern. Add in the late stumbles from last season and the winless run at home in the league is now four games.

For a club that built title challenges on suffocating home intensity, those returns are poor. There is no need to dress it up.

Two recent performances could have ended even worse. Liverpool needed major interventions from Jeremy Jacquet in both matches to avoid defeat. When your centre-back is repeatedly acting as the emergency brake at home, something in the overall structure is off.

The criticism from Paul Scholes and Nicky Butt will not be welcomed by many Liverpool supporters, but it is hard to dismiss. Speaking alongside James Milner , both pointed to the same issue, Anfield no longer feels like the same ordeal for visiting sides.

Scholes put it plainly: "When you go to Liverpool, especially when James was there, when Jurgen Klopp was there, the crowd played such a major part. It feels like that's gone… I don't think the fans are quite on board at the minute with what's happening there.

"When we used to go there, I'd think, 'Bloody hell, how are we going to get the ball?', because they were on top of you. Teams seem to have a lot more possession and look a bit more comfortable than they ever have."

That is the key point. Opposition teams are getting time on the ball. They are settling into games. They are not being swallowed by the environment. Anfield has not become easy, but it has become manageable, and that is a major change.

Butt made a similar point, and again there is not much room for argument. He said: "The likes of Fulham five years ago are going to Anfield and they're beaten before they even go up the steps. You see them looking across at James' team and they're going, 'How am I going to compete with these?'

"When you lose that and you give them a little bit of hope, they're thinking, 'I'm playing at Anfield. I want these to come and buy me, so I'm going to go and show how good I am'. That transpires right through the team and you end up with results like you're getting."

Anfield atmosphere and team performance are tied together

This is where the discussion usually becomes emotional. It should stay practical. Atmosphere does matter, but it does not exist in a vacuum. Crowds respond to what they see. If the football is flat, predictable or hesitant, the stadium will reflect it.

That does not let supporters off the hook entirely. A ground like Anfield has always prided itself on driving the team through difficult moments. But the relationship runs both ways. The players need to give the crowd something to latch onto, intensity, aggression, risk, purpose. Without that, frustration spreads quickly.

The sight of supporters heading for the exits early against Fulham did not go unnoticed. Nor should it. For years, opponents talked about surviving the opening 15 minutes at Anfield. Now they are talking about growing into games there. That is a serious shift in psychology.

Liverpool have already dropped more points at home inside the first month of this campaign than they did in the entire 2019-20 title-winning season. Those are not decorative statistics, they define standards. Right now, those standards are not being met.

Andoni Iraola is still early in the job, but that buys only limited patience at a club of this size. Home form is the fastest way to shape the mood around a team, and the mood matters. If Anfield becomes anxious, every misplaced pass feels heavier, every delay in tempo becomes more obvious, every opponent gains encouragement.

Liverpool's next home fixtures have to start changing the narrative. Tottenham Hotspur arriving without a goal this season should present an opportunity. No one needs a grand statement. They need a convincing display, control of the game, intensity without the ball and enough quality to finish the job.

This does not require nostalgia for Klopp's best days. It requires a reset in basics. Start fast. Press properly. Move the ball with purpose. Make opponents feel under siege again.

Anfield still has the history, the size and the symbolism. What it lacks at the moment is menace. Until Liverpool restore that, teams will keep turning up believing they can take something, and too often, they will be right.

articles.title: Week 2 has Justin Jefferson set to make Vikings history
articles.summary: Justin Jefferson has a chance at Minnesota Vikings history next week against the Chicago Bears.
articles.body:
Justin Jefferson enjoyed a vintage performance on Sunday, as he had his best game in ages, going for 8 receptions for 92 yards and two touchdowns, including a two-point conversion. He had his first touchdown at home and his first two-touchdown performance since November 2024. This was exactly the type of game we needed to see from Jefferson, and it left him on the doorstep of Vikings history next week.

With just one reception next week against the Chicago Bears , Jefferson will pass Randy Moss to become second in all-time Vikings receptions, as Moss has 587. Jefferson is on pace to pass Cris Carter's 1,004 receptions before his career is over, and could easily fly past that total.

Jefferson currently sits outside the top 100 in all-time receptions, but given that he is already that high up the rankings at just 27 years old, he could easily end his career inside the top ten, or even give the top guys a run for their money.

articles.title: Kirk Herbstreit rips AP voters for dropping Ohio State to No. 6: 'I don't agree with it'
articles.summary: ESPN analyst Kirk Herbstreit ripped AP poll voters for dropping Ohio State from No. 1 to No. 6 after the Buckeyes' 24-23 loss at Texas.
articles.body:
Following Ohio State 's heartbreaking 24-23 loss to Texas on Saturday, Sept. 12, the Buckeyes fell from No. 1 to No. 6 in the Associated Press poll.

To one of the most prominent voices in college football — and a former Ohio State quarterback, to boot — it was too steep of a drop.

On his podcast on Monday, Sept. 14, ESPN analyst Kirk Herbstreit ripped AP voters for dropping the Buckeyes as far as they did, noting that — while the loss was demoralizing — a road defeat against a top-five opponent didn't merit a five-spot fall-off.

"I don't agree with it," Herbstreit said . "Ohio State was No. 1 coming into the game. They played really well for three quarters. And then the game, to Texas' credit, Texas beat Ohio State. People can say all they want about how Ohio State got conservative, they played not to lose, whatever the case may be. They were dominating a football game 23-3 heading into the fourth quarter, and Texas comes back to win the game.

"Yeah, you should be penalized for losing a game, but it's kind of silly to drop all the way down to six after playing the way they did coming in at No. 1."

Who's at the Ohio State-Texas football game? See celebrity photos

After the win, Texas rose to No. 1 in both the US LBM Coaches Poll and the AP Top 25. The Longhorns were fourth in the AP poll heading into the game at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin, Texas. The Buckeyes also fell to No. 6 in the Coaches Poll, putting them behind, in order, Texas, Georgia, Notre Dame, Indiana and Miami.

Coach Ryan Day's team led by 20, 23-3, early in the fourth quarter before Texas stormed back to score 21 points in the final 14:19. The Longhorns scored touchdowns on each of their final three drives after managing only a field goal through their first eight possessions.

Despite the loss, the Buckeyes outgained Texas by a 372-336 margin and held the Longhorns to just 4.3 yards per play.

Longhorns coach Steve Sarkisian was even more effusive than Herbstreit, saying on Monday that Ohio State should "be rewarded for playing in this game against us."

As with any Ohio State loss, particularly one that unfolded the way it did, Day has received a significant amount of criticism from a fan base with justifiably high expectations. But to Herbstreit, the Buckeyes' shortcomings shouldn't have dropped them out of the top five and attributed it to an outdated philosophy from the poll's voters.

"If they dropped [Ohio State] to 3 I think that would make sense maybe, 2 or 3," Herbstreit said. "I just don't understand how they go, that's just like a 1970s way of polling. It makes no sense to me at all, but I think it'll work itself out."

articles.title: No team scored fewer points than the Rams in Week 1
articles.summary: After leading the NFL in points a season ago, the Rams are currently last in scoring so far in 2026.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams had no trouble moving the ball or putting up points last season, leading the NFL in scoring and total yards. Unfortunately, that momentum didn't carry over into 2026 because through one week, the Rams are the lowest-scoring team in the league.

In their loss to the San Francisco 49ers , the Rams only scored seven points , losing 27-7 in Melbourne. In what was a record-tying Week 1 for scoring with 791 total points across the league, the Rams put up the fewest points of any team.

Four other teams only scored 10 points, but the Rams were the only ones not to reach double digits in the opening week of the season. The Patriots, Titans, Broncos and Browns all tied for the second-fewest points with 10.

The Rams' seven points are the fewest they've ever scored in Week 1 under Sean McVay. Their previous low was in 2022 when they scored just 10 against the Bills . The last time they scored fewer than 10 points was in 2016, a 28-0 loss to the 49ers. It was only the fifth time the Rams failed to hit double digits in Week 1 since 1994.

It's not that they were totally anemic on offense. They had 290 total yards, which ranked 19th in the opening week. The Vikings, for comparison, scored 39 points on just 239 yards of total offense. The Rams just had an interception in 49ers territory, a fumble at their own 39 and turned it over on downs when Matthew Stafford was stuffed on fourth-and-goal from the 1.

Week 1 is the most misleading week of the season, and surely the Rams won't finish near the bottom of the league in scoring this season. But for at least one week, they're alone in the basement.

articles.title: Mets news: Devin Williams may still return from injury this season
articles.summary: The New York Mets are missing the postseason for the second consecutive year. Even though New York’s National League team doesn’t have much left to play for,...
articles.body:
The New York Mets are missing the postseason for the second consecutive year. Even though New York 's National League team doesn't have much left to play for, it appears reliever Devin Williams may soon return. The reliever has been dealing with a shoulder strain .

"(Williams) continued his mound work with a Sept. 14 bullpen session at Citi Field. Expects to throw another on Sept. 17. Could be activated two or three days after that," MLB.com reported.

The Mets reliever has been out of the bullpen since August. He has 16 saves this season and holds a 4.66 ERA for New York. Williams has appeared in 42 games.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

This is Williams' first season with the Mets. He spent the 2025 campaign with the New York Yankees , where he struggled. Williams finished that campaign with six losses and a 4.79 ERA.

Williams is not the only Mets pitcher looking to return from injury. So is left-hander Cionel Perez , who is dealing with a forearm strain. Perez is also expected to return before the end of the year.

Mets are looking to make change after this year

New York has had a disaster of a year. Despite having a large payroll and lots of talent on the roster including Juan Soto , the club just wasn't able to win enough games this season. The Mets are currently 69-81 on the campaign.

The team will be looking for a new manager for the 2027 campaign. Carlos Mendoza was fired after the team got out to a rough start to the year. Mendoza had led the team to the NLCS in 2024, but the club had little success after that.

New York plays the Baltimore Orioles on Tuesday. This Mets-Orioles series marks the return of former Mets star Pete Alonso to Queens . Alonso now plays for Baltimore.

The Mets have wins in six of their last 10 games.

articles.title: Steph Curry’s Golf Game Crushes Most Pro Athlete Hype
articles.summary: Forget the hype about athletes trying their hand at golf. Most of them just look good in the photos. Steph Curry is the real deal, and the gap between him an...
articles.body:
Forget the hype about athletes trying their hand at golf. Most of them just look good in the photos. Steph Curry is the real deal, and the gap between him and other famous names is massive. According to MyGolfSpy, Curry sits right around scratch to plus-1, which puts him in elite territory for anyone outside the pro tour. This isn't a weekend warrior story. It is a serious athletic crossover that deserves respect.

Many people assume Tony Romo or Charles Barkley are the kings of celebrity golf. That assumption is dead wrong. Romo technically has a lower handicap, but Curry plays with a competitive edge that Romo simply does not match during the NBA season. MyGolfSpy reported that Romo floats in the plus-1 to plus-3 range, while Curry holds a tighter grip on scratch play. If they played an 18-hole match, Curry would wipe the floor with him. The consistency required to maintain a plus-handicap while playing 82 NBA games is a feat few can claim. Curry brings a level of focus that separates him from the pack.

Some might argue that playing golf on a Tuesday afternoon is different from a real test. The numbers say otherwise. In 2017, Curry stepped onto the Korn Ferry Tour and fired back-to-back rounds of 74. That performance nearly made the cut, missing by just 11 strokes. To put that in perspective, the winner of that tournament finished 18-under across four days. That is a brutal field. Curry didn't just show up; he competed against players who make their living on the course. He is likely much better than the average fan thinks.

Curry's golf skills are getting a commercial boost with a new partnership. Curry Brand is entering a new chapter with Li-Ning, a massive $4-billion company. Within this ecosystem, Steph joins stars like Jimmy Butler and Dwyane Wade as the first to unveil a golf shoe. The design leans more European and will definitely ruffle some feathers among die-hard fans. MyGolfSpy noted that the initial thoughts point straight to the adidas MC87 as a design comparison. Although a release date for this specific shoe has yet to be announced, the plans are clear. This move signals that Curry takes his game seriously enough to build a brand around it.

Most athletes treat golf as a hobby. Curry treats it like a second career. He is a player who will take your lunch money any day of the week, not only the best three-point shooter of all time.

articles.title: Backlash after Texas QB Arch Manning calls AI video of Sarkisian hitting Rowe 'hilarious'
articles.summary: Two days after leading the Texas football team to a dramatic win over Ohio State, senior quarterback Arch Manning received criticism for comments he made to...
articles.body:
Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning is receiving criticism for comments he made Monday about an AI-generated video that featured his head coach and ESPN reporter Holly Rowe.

During his weekly media availability, Manning was asked if he had seen any online videos that had been posted about Saturday night's postgame scene at Royal-Memorial Stadium. Manning said he had seen an AI-edited video about the abrupt interview between Texas coach Steve Sarkisian and Rowe following the Longhorns' 24-23 win over Ohio State .

After his response received some laughter and goading from media members, Manning smiled as he asked: "Y'all seen that one? That's a good one. Of him slapping Holly Rowe? Yeah, it's hilarious."

Once again, laughter became audible in a room of reporters much older than the 22-year-old Manning.

The AI-generated video that Manning referenced featured Sarkisian ending his interview with a backhanded slap of Rowe, a veteran ESPN reporter. In reality, Sarkisian walked away from a visibly annoyed Rowe after saying, "Let's go, Texas fight! Hook 'Em."

Due to the violence depicted in the fake video, both Manning's comments and the subsequent reaction of reporters were denounced by many on social media. Some users, however, used their platforms to defend Manning and argue that the exchange was misunderstood.

As of Tuesday morning, Texas had not responded to an American-Statesman inquiry about the comment or a clarification. Manning had not addressed the incident either.

Sarkisian was not asked about his interaction with Rowe during a 30-minute availability Monday. Over the weekend, a UT spokesperson told The Athletic that technical difficulties were a factor in the awkward exchange between Sarkisian and Rowe.

Texas (2-0) will play UTSA (2-0) at home on Saturday night . The Longhorns are ranked No. 1 in the Associated Press poll .
